key_insight: CLExEval shows that LLM clinical reasoning can look convincing in explanation while still being wrong in diagnosis, especially when information is limited or presentation is verbose.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI evaluation, expert-verified reasoning checks are needed because automated judges and surface-level explanations can substantially overestimate clinical reliability.
method: Built a human-in-the-loop evaluation framework for clinical reasoning
Used progressive information masking to test how diagnosis changes as details are removed
Combined 5,600 physician annotations with 200 reasoning traces from 40 rare diagnostic cases
evidence_signal: In the abstract, GPT-4o-mini’s diagnostic accuracy fell from 95.0% to 32.5% under information scarcity, and the judge model approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs in a human-verified failure set (n=142).
watch_item: Results come from rare-case traces and expert-labeled evaluations, so generalization to broader clinical settings and different model families still needs careful validation.
paper_title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
